fix(functions): prevent hung promises when refreshing expired source tokens (#11255)

### Description
When a previously scraped Cloud Functions source token expired during a deployment, `SourceTokenScraper.getToken()` awaited the existing token promise before checking expiration. This allowed concurrent function deployments to overwrite the refresh promise and leave waiting deployments unresolved, causing the CLI to exit early with code `0` instead of completing the deployment.

This change checks token expiration synchronously before awaiting the promise so concurrent callers share the refreshed token promise.

Part of #6989

### Scenarios Tested
- Unit test verifying that concurrent `SourceTokenScraper.getToken()` calls on an expired token share a single refresh without hanging waiters.

### Sample Commands
```bash
firebase deploy --only functions
```

fix(throttler): continue draining queued tasks after a task fails (#11248)

When a throttled task exhausted its retries or timed out, `Throttler` did not schedule the next waiting task into the freed concurrency slot. During Cloud Functions deployments, if all active concurrency slots failed, remaining queued functions were never scheduled and the CLI exited early with code `0` instead of reporting deployment errors.

This change ensures the throttler continues processing queued tasks after a task failure.

Part of #6989
Part of #11040

- Unit tests verifying that `Throttler` and `QueueExecutor` continue draining queued tasks after retry exhaustion or task timeouts.

description:
Add firebase init run interactive setup (#11204)

* Add firebase init run interactive setup

* Use directcloudrun experiment and validate rootDir is a directory

* Trim baseImage input in init run

* Improve readability of firebase init run and remove mainContainer

* Use dirExistsSync from fsutils in init run promptRootDir

* Don't default to a base image in init run

A base image turns on automatic base image updates, which are off by default. So init no longer suggests nodejs22. An existing service still defaults to its own base image.

* Make upsertRunConfig easier to read

Spell out what init changes on an existing service (rootDir and region) instead of merging three spreads. upsertRunConfig now adds the default ignore list itself, so actuate no longer passes it. Behavior is unchanged; added a test for the ignore fallback on existing services.

* Don't add an ignore list to an existing service in init run

Re-running init on a service that's already in firebase.json filled in the default ignore list when the entry didn't have one. Init doesn't ask about ignore, so it shouldn't change it: an existing entry now only gets the rootDir and region the user just chose. New services still get the default ignore list.

* Default init run's root directory to the saved one, matching by service ID and region

Pressing Enter now keeps the root directory saved in firebase.json instead of resetting it to /. Cloud Run service IDs are only unique within a region, so entries now match on both; the same ID in another region gets its own entry.

* Write firebase.json once, from init, instead of also from init run's actuate

Init already writes firebase.json after every feature is set up, so the write in actuate only printed "Wrote configuration info to firebase.json" a second time. Leaving the write to init also means a failed init leaves firebase.json untouched.

v1.1.11 · 2026-09-23

  1. Proxy-CLI 接入 16 个火山引擎产品 CLI

    在 ve arkcli、ve tosutil 基础上扩展为统一的产品代理入口，当前版本内置 16 个可直接调用（ready）的产品原生命令，覆盖对象存储 TOS（tosutil、ve-tos-cli）、火山方舟 Ark（arkcli）、日志服务（volclog）、函数服务 veFaaS（vefaas）、智能网盘（ve-adrive-cli）、流式计算 Flink（volc-flink）、AI 原生 BaaS Supabase（byted-supabase-cli）、向量数据库 Milvus（milvus-cli）、Viking 知识库（viking-cli）、AI MediaKit（mediakit-cli）、实时音视频 RTC（vertc）、边缘函数（nest）、可观测 VeOps（veops-cli）、国际化翻译 Starling（starling）和 OpenViking（ov）。产品命令后的参数原样转发，标准输入、输出与退出码保持产品原有语义，认证与 profile 配置继续遵循各产品自身规则。

  2. 新增产品目录发现与托管管理命令

    新增 ve proxycli list 和 ve proxycli info <产品ID>，查看当前版本支持的产品、调用入口、支持平台与官方文档；ve proxycli install/upgrade <产品ID> 用于预装或升级托管程序（upgrade 支持 --yes 跳过确认），也可通过 ve proxycli run <产品ID> -- <参数> 按产品 ID 显式调用。管理命令使用产品 ID（如 TLS 的 ID 为 tls-cli，调用入口为 ve volclog），仅 ready 状态的产品可以调用；Agent 可通过 ve proxycli list --output json 读取目录后再按各产品文档调用。

  3. 按需单文件安装，加固下载来源与并发安装

    产品 CLI 与 VE 宿主独立分发：默认安装 VE 不会下载任何产品工具，首次调用某个产品能力时才下载对应的单文件程序并校验 SHA-256，之后复用本地程序；系统 PATH 中已存在原生程序时优先使用，外部安装仍由原包管理器维护。下载地址限定在内置可信来源白名单内，并发首次安装只会发布一个完整程序；在线清单不可用时回退到内嵌固定版本清单。

  4. 普通 OpenAPI 请求统一携带持久化客户端标识

    X-Client-Id 请求头从此前的 ve docs search/fetch 扩展到全部普通 OpenAPI 请求，包括 --force 调用和 MCP 工具发起的 API 调用。请求头在签名前设置，GET、表单 POST 和 JSON POST 均会携带，不会出现在 URL 查询参数或请求体中，也不改变 User-Agent 与输出格式。标识仍为首次请求时生成的 UUIDv4（122 位随机熵），持久化在 ~/.volcengine/client_id（Windows 为 %USERPROFILE%\.volcengine\client_id），重启、升级、登录或切换 profile 后保持不变；无法读取、保存或校验标识时请求直接报错，不发送没有稳定标识的请求。通过 --header 传入的同名请求头会被本地持久化标识覆盖；ve arkcli、ve tosutil（含 ve toscli）等代理执行不生成或注入该标识。

  5. skills-setup v0.9.0 仅引导安装 ve

    技能初始化不再单独安装 @volcengine/ark-cli，方舟 CLI 统一通过 ve arkcli 按需获取，避免重复安装以及全局 bin 已存在时的安装冲突。

使用示例：

ve proxycli list
ve proxycli info tls-cli
ve volclog --help
ve milvus-cli version
ve proxycli install tls-cli
ve proxycli upgrade tls-cli --yes

Minor Changes

  • #16036 9a58244 Thanks @edevil! - Support temporary event accounts in R2 and Containers commands

    wrangler r2 and wrangler containers commands now accept the hidden --temporary flag, so accounts created for an event can manage buckets, objects and containers directly. Every command that supports --temporary now also accepts a hidden --event-code flag, so the first command a participant runs can create the event account:

    wrangler r2 bucket create my-bucket --temporary --event-code

    R2 and Containers are only available on event accounts. R2 custom domains, Sippy, external container registries and wrangler cloudchamber commands still require a logged-in account.

Patch Changes

  • #16139 2d1d563 Thanks @cpojer! - Update esbuild to 0.28.2

    Align esbuild dependency with tooling using the latest 0.28 patch so package managers can share one installation instead of downloading a second native binary.

  • #15632 85b14e7 Thanks @petebacondarwin! - Honor Retry-After directives during static asset uploads

    Static asset uploads now pause retries and pending uploads until the latest outstanding deadline requested by the API. A per-request limiter also keeps gateway retries at the reduced concurrency after the pause ends, preventing a deployment from immediately overloading a constrained asset service again.

  • #16098 fe607f9 Thanks @dependabot! - Update dependencies of "miniflare", "wrangler"

    The following dependency versions have been updated:

    Dependency From To
    sharp 0.35.4 0.35.5

  • #16093 ad7ff45 Thanks @DiogoSantoss! - Document that addresses catch-all entries must use the zone apex

    A *@domain entry in addresses must use the zone apex, such as *@example.com. The zone catch-all also receives mail for every subdomain in the zone that has no literal rule.

  • #16102 757faa6 Thanks @tlq5l! - Keep Preview secrets when deploying to an existing Preview

    Secrets added to a Preview with wrangler preview secret put or wrangler preview secret bulk were lost the next time wrangler preview ran, because each new deployment was created from the Wrangler config, --var and --secrets-file values only.

    wrangler preview now carries over the secrets of the Preview's latest deployment. A value passed in this deployment (--secrets-file, --var or a previews binding with the same name) still replaces the existing secret, and wrangler preview secret delete removes one.

  • #15617 93c1069 Thanks @jpatel3! - Stop the update check from recommending deprecated versions

    Previously, the "update available" notice shown by wrangler and @cloudflare/vite-plugin always pointed at whichever version was tagged latest on npm, even after that version had been deprecated for shipping a bug. Deprecated versions are now never recommended: if the latest release has been deprecated, the newest non-deprecated stable release below it is suggested instead, or nothing at all if you are already on it.

    The check now reads the npm registry directly instead of going through the update-check package, which discarded the deprecation information. The on-disk cache location and one-hour refresh interval are unchanged.

  • #16003 6947df3 Thanks @oddharsh! - Ship using and await using declarations to the runtime as written, for smaller Worker bundles

    Workers and Pages Functions that use explicit resource management no longer carry about 1 KB of bundled helper code to emulate it. workerd supports using and await using natively at every compatibility date, so wrangler deploy, wrangler versions upload and Pages Functions builds now leave these declarations untouched.

  • #15958 82acf3c Thanks @breken-ai! - Apply each action's own condition in wrangler r2 bucket lifecycle add

    When a lifecycle rule was added with both expiration and Infrequent Access transition flags, both actions read their condition from the same list of flags, which checked --expire-days first. --expire-days 365 --ia-transition-days 30 therefore transitioned objects after 365 days instead of 30, and --expire-date 2027-01-01 --ia-transition-days 30 deleted objects after 30 days instead of on the given date. Expiration now only reads --expire-days/--expire-date, and transition only reads --ia-transition-days/--ia-transition-date.

    • miniflare@5.20261006.1-alpha

    Align esbuild dependency with tooling using the latest 0.28 patch so package managers can share one installation instead of downloading a second native binary.

  • #15939 e6f7663 Thanks @00200200! - Fix local Workflows hitting the timer quota on long runs

    Long local workflows no longer fail from timer exhaustion. Step timeout timers, sleep, waitForEvent, and grace-period waits now cancel their underlying timers when finished or aborted, instead of remaining until their original deadlines.

  • #16098 fe607f9 Thanks @dependabot! - Update dependencies of "miniflare", "wrangler"

  • #15879 8de6b3c Thanks @dawNotPoi! - Stop Hyperdrive proxy listeners from accumulating across local development reloads

    Miniflare now reuses a listener when a Hyperdrive binding keeps the same target and closes listeners no longer used after a configuration update. Changing or removing a binding, including switching to sslmode=disable, no longer leaves stale listening ports in wrangler dev.

  • #16106 ae29445 Thanks @Arthur031221! - Fix the local Images binding and cf.image transforms ignoring EXIF orientation. Previously, photos stored with an EXIF orientation flag (e.g. phone portrait photos, stored as landscape pixels plus a rotation flag) came back sideways from local transforms, while the production Images binding auto-orients them. Local dev now bakes the EXIF rotation into the pixels before applying transforms, matching production behavior.

  • #16041 cc8e969 Thanks @Shubham-Padkonde! - Support single-object R2 deletion through the Local Explorer API

    Local R2 clients can now delete an object with DELETE /r2/buckets/{bucket_name}/objects/{object_key} instead of having to use the bulk-delete endpoint. The route handles path-like keys and uses the same storage service as other local R2 operations.

  • #16144 417b186 Thanks @cpojer! - Honor the source-map setting in release builds

    Previously, the "update available" notice shown by wrangler and @cloudflare/vite-plugin always pointed at whichever version was tagged latest on npm, even after that version had been deprecated for shipping a bug. description:
Format and highlight EXPLAIN (SQL) output (#26288)

`EXPLAIN (SQL)` produces SQL that can be executed again, but its
unformatted output becomes difficult to read as the generated query
grows. Autocomplete already exposes a SQL formatter, and the CLI already
has SQL syntax highlighting, so I reuse those facilities here.

I format the returned SQL when autocomplete is already loaded, using the
same defaults as `duckdb_format_sql`. This applies to all clients and
adds line breaks between clauses. Without autocomplete loaded, the
existing unformatted output is preserved. `EXPLAIN` does not install or
load the extension, and the formatting choice is made when the statement
is planned.

In the CLI, I route SQL explain output through the existing highlighter,
respecting `.highlight` and terminal detection. I also skip the plan
tree setup for SQL explain and measure the SQL's rendered dimensions
when deciding whether to use the pager, rather than relying on the width
of a previous plan. API results and redirected output remain plain SQL.

Using the formatter on executable SQL also exposes a problem in its
later text-processing passes: they can treat newlines and punctuation
inside quoted content as SQL structure. I make those passes respect
token boundaries so multiline string values and quoted identifiers
retain their contents, including when expanding CASE expressions,
argument lists, and CREATE TABLE definitions.

Task scheduler threads should use a ConsumerToken to improve query execution fairness (#26809)

When a running a query, DuckDB converts the physical plan into a series
of tasks that are then scheduled for execution using the TaskScheduler.
Each task is (optionally partially) executed and may spawn new tasks, or
reschedule itself for future execution.

Without any hard guarantees, it is expected that task will be picked up
for execution in somewhat fairly manner, preventing one task from being
starved by submitting new tasks to the scheduler. That is sadly not the
case today.

The reason lies in the internal semantics of the moodycamel library,
Today, each query is associated with a so called producer (a sub queue
in the scheduler), and all the tasks submitted to the scheduler by the
query is put into it's producer queue. The application thread that
submitted the query typically participates with the query execution by
picking up tasks only from that specific queue, but queries are often
assisted by the worker threads which pick up tasks and execute them in
the background.

Today, the worker threads just ask for the next task from moodycamel. To
choose one moodycamel first needs to choose a producer queue, and then
hand out a task from it. To do so, moodycamel walks the first 3 (!) non
empty producers in a linked list it maintains and chooses the largest
queue from that:

```
	template
	bool try_dequeue(U& item)
	{
		// Instead of simply trying each producer in turn (which could cause needless contention on the first
		// producer), we score them heuristically.
		size_t nonEmptyCount = 0;
		ProducerBase* best = nullptr;
		size_t bestSize = 0;
		for (auto ptr = producerListTail.load(std::memory_order_acquire); nonEmptyCount < 3 && ptr != nullptr; ptr = ptr->next_prod()) {
			auto size = ptr->size_approx();
			if (size > 0) {
				if (size > bestSize) {
					bestSize = size;
					best = ptr;
				}
				++nonEmptyCount;
			}
		}
```

That seems reasonable (although the number of 3 is fairly arbitrary) but
it becomes a problem when combined with two other things moodycamel
does:

1) Every new producer is put at the tail of the queue (the tail is
consulted *first* , why it's not called a head is beyond me).
2) When a query completes, producers are not cleaned up, but rather are
kept around empty, and are re-used, starting from the tail.

This means that newer queries tend to be put in the queue ahead of
existing old queries, and thus get unfair preferential treatment.

Luckily, moodycamel has a construct call ConsumerToken that aims to deal
with this problem, even if the lock free nature of the system makes it
really hard and imprecise to reason about fairness. Roughly, it does:
1) Have each worker maintain a position in the producer list.
2) Worker move to the next producer if their current producer is
finished.
3) Every N operations (per worker), a random "noise" is introduced
(called rotation) triggering force change of produces by the worker.

This PR changes the workers to use this mechanism.

## Concrete changes

- Worker threads (`ExecuteForever`) and external threads
(`ExecuteTasks`, used by `duckdb_execute_tasks`) dequeue through a
moodycamel `ConsumerToken`, wrapped in a new DuckDB `ConsumerToken` that
mirrors `ProducerToken` (one token per pool queue). A thread keeps
dequeuing from its current producer and moves on to the next one after a
quota of tasks, so every producer gets a turn.
- The token-less `TaskSchedulerQueue::Dequeue` and the unused
`GetTaskInternal(task, pool_type)` are removed.
- The quota (`EXPLICIT_CONSUMER_CONSUMPTION_QUOTA_BEFORE_ROTATE`) is
lowered from moodycamel's default of 256 to 16, to recognize that DuckDB
tasks are heavier and take a bit to complete.

### Why 16

To be honest, that is an arbitrary number - just like the default 256.
The quota only bounds how many steps a query keeps a worker before the
next query gets a turn, and 256 steps is more than a typical query takes
in total, so with 256 , queries running are not likely to trigger a
rotation (the counter is reset every time a work depletes a processor -
i.e, a query).

Here's the result of a simulation where a short query is submitted
before 3 heavy ones, with 1 worker, `scheduler_process_partial=true`,
and all queries only polled. Time until the short query finishes:

| heavy query | v2.0 | token, quota 256 | token, quota 16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sum(hash(i))` over 30M rows (~290 steps of ~0.5 ms) | 449 ms | 452 ms
| 64 ms |
| `md5(i::VARCHAR) LIKE '%abc%'` over 10M rows (~100 steps of ~14 ms) |
4.0 s | 4.1 s | 1.7 s |

As you can see, the change isn't effective (getting the short query to
complete earlier then the heavy query) unless we reduce the number



Benchmark code

Built against the shared library (`clang++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Isrc/include
bench.cpp -Lbuild/reldebug/src -lduckdb`) and run as `./bench 1 3 hash`
and `./bench 1 3 md5`. The quota is a compile-time trait, so each column
is a separate build.

```cpp
// A short query is submitted first, then N heavy queries; all are polled only (no client thread executes tasks).
// Prints how long the short query took and when each heavy query finished, relative to the workers starting.
#include "duckdb.hpp"
#include "duckdb/parallel/task_scheduler.hpp"

#include 
#include 
#include 
#include 

using namespace duckdb;

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	idx_t workers = argc > 1 ? std::atoi(argv[1]) : 1;
	idx_t heavy_count = argc > 2 ? std::atoi(argv[2]) : 3;
	const char *short_query = "SELECT sum(i) FROM range(1000000) t(i)";
	string kind = argc > 3 ? argv[3] : "hash";
	string heavy_query = kind == "hash" ? "SELECT sum(hash(i)) FROM range(30000000) t(i)"
	                                     : "SELECT count(*) FROM range(10000000) t(i) WHERE md5(i::VARCHAR) LIKE '%abc%'";

	// hold the workers back until every query is submitted, so the short query has the oldest producer
	DBConfig config;
	config.options.maximum_threads = workers + 1;
	config.SetOptionByName("external_threads", Value::UBIGINT(workers + 1));
	DuckDB db(nullptr, &config);
	Connection setup(db);
	setup.Query("SET scheduler_process_partial=true")->ThrowIfError();

	vector> connections;
	vector> results;
	for (idx_t i = 0; i <= heavy_count; i++) {
		connections.push_back(make_uniq(db));
		results.push_back(connections.back()->Submit(i == 0 ? short_query : heavy_query));
		results.back()->ThrowIfError();
		results.back()->Materialize();
	}
	setup.Query("SET external_threads=1")->ThrowIfError();
	TaskScheduler::GetScheduler(*db.instance).RelaunchThreads();

	auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
	vector finished(results.size(), -1);
	idx_t remaining = results.size();
	while (remaining > 0) {
		for (idx_t i = 0; i < results.size(); i++) {
			if (finished[i] < 0 && IsTerminal(results[i]->Poll())) {
				results[i]->ThrowIfError();
				finished[i] = std::chrono::duration(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count();
				remaining--;
			}
		}
		std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(200));
	}
	printf("workers=%llu heavy=%llu x %-5s short=%6.0fms heavy:", (unsigned long long)workers,
	       (unsigned long long)heavy_count, kind.c_str(), finished[0]);
	for (idx_t i = 1; i < finished.size(); i++) {
		printf(" %6.0fms", finished[i]);
	}
	printf("\n");
	return 0;
}
```




## Test

`test/api/test_scheduler_fairness.cpp` runs a single worker with
`scheduler_process_partial=true`. Three newer `TaskExecutor`s (each has
its own producer, like a query's `Executor`) keep the worker busy with
tasks that never finish, and an older `TaskExecutor` schedules a short
task. Before this change the short task never runs and the test hits its
5 s deadline; with it, the test passes in about 10 ms.

fix(dev): use URL separators for static file paths (#8593)

## Problem

`netlify dev` returns 403 on Windows for static files that need a
redirect
shadow check, such as paths with spaces or brackets. `getStatic` builds
the
URL forwarded to the static server with `path.relative`, which yields
backslashes on Windows, so the static server receives
`/files%5Cfile%20with%20spaces.html`.

This has been latent since 2020. `@fastify/static` 10.1.4
(GHSA-r799-r9gc-m956)
added a path spelling guard that splits on `/`, stats the joined path,
finds
the file under a different spelling, and rejects it. Earlier versions
served
the file.

Surfaced by the Windows integration shard on #8575, which fails
`should not shadow an existing file that has unsafe URL characters` on
every
attempt. The previous five release PRs passed it.

## Approach

Split the relative path on `path.sep` and join with `/`, so the URL
always
uses forward slashes. Only OS separators are rewritten; a literal
backslash in
a POSIX filename is preserved.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck`, `npx eslint src/utils/proxy.ts`, `npm run build`:
clean
- `npm exec vitest -- run tests/integration/commands/dev/dev.test.ts`
with
  `@fastify/static` 10.1.5 installed: 27 passed

Verified on macOS only, where `path.relative` already returns forward
slashes,
so this run cannot reproduce the bug. PRs do not run Windows integration
tests. The proof is the Windows shard on the regenerated release PR
after
this merges.

## Risk

Low. One-line change on the path the proxy already controls. No behavior
change on POSIX, where `path.sep` is already `/`.

## Rollback

Revert this commit.

[`51c2733`](https://redirect.github.com/verdaccio/verdaccio/commit/51c2733):
Expose the optional legacy authentication cache for Verdaccio 6.x
through `server.legacyAuthCache`.

This feature is intended for performance-sensitive installations that
still use legacy bearer tokens. When enabled, Verdaccio caches
successful legacy token authentication results for a short period of
time, so repeated requests using the same token do not need to run
password verification through the authentication plugin every time.
Concurrent requests for the same legacy token can also share the same
in-flight authentication result.

The cache is disabled by default, so existing installations keep their
current authentication behavior unless they explicitly opt in. Basic
authentication is not cached. If the cache is enabled, changed or
revoked credentials may remain valid until the cached entry expires.

  Enable it in `config.yaml`:

  ```yaml
  server:
    legacyAuthCache:
      enabled: true
      ttlMs: 15000
      maxEntries: 1000
  ```

  Options:

- `enabled`: enables the legacy token authentication cache. Default:
`false`.
- `ttlMs`: time in milliseconds before a cached validation expires.
Default: `15000`.
- `maxEntries`: maximum number of cached legacy tokens. Default: `1000`.

v4.1.0


This minor release upgrades the SAX parser and introduces stricter
XML validation. It also includes important security hardening for
removeScripts, dependency updates, and improvements to the
test and regression infrastructure.


Support SVGO


If SVGO is valuable to you or your organization, please consider supporting the project on
OpenCollective. Your sponsorship helps fund ongoing maintenance and
security work.


Stricter XML validation


SVGO now uses sax 1.6.1,
upgraded from 1.5.0 (#2257).


The new parser version validates numeric character references against
the ranges permitted by XML. Invalid references are now rejected in both
text and attributes, including:


    

  • disallowed control characters such as
&[#1](https://github.com/svg/svgo/issues/1);,
, and ;
    • 

  • UTF-16 surrogate code points such as �;
    • 

  • invalid XML code points such as .
    • 



Valid boundary values—including U+0020,
U+D7FF, U+E000, U+FFFD, and
characters through U+10FFFF—remain supported.


Parser failures are consistently exposed as
SvgoParserError errors with an Invalid character
entity reason.


This is an intentional behavior change: malformed SVGs that were
previously accepted may now produce a parser error, while valid XML
documents are unaffected.


Security


The removeScripts
plugin has been hardened against several script-execution bypasses:


    

  • Filters executable data: URLs containing HTML, XHTML,
or SVG documents while preserving inert data such as PNG images, and
filters legacy vbscript: URLs (#2263).
    • 

  • Sanitizes content inside SVG <foreignObject>
elements by removing HTML event-handler attributes, srcdoc,
and executable URLs from action, data,
formaction, href, and src, while
preserving non-executable HTML and visual content (#2264).
    • 

  • Recognizes namespace-prefixed SVG <a> elements
and removes ASCII tabs and newlines before checking URL schemes,
preventing values such as
java&[#9](https://github.com/svg/svgo/issues/9);script:
from bypassing detection while preserving elements in unrelated custom
namespaces (#2268).

v7, and updated SVGO's custom selector adapter for
css-select v6 (#2244).

Project maintenance

back as an active SVGO maintainer.


Many thanks to @​KTibow, @​SethFalco, and @​XhmikosR for
maintaining and improving SVGO over the past several years.

v1.9.0


Huge update!!! This is most likely the largest
update the library received since its release, with lots of new features
and improvements.


Performance improvements


Significant parts of the internal parse logic have been rewritten,
improving performance by 1.5x-2x. The library was
already comfortably ahead of the others, but it is now faster than ever,
sitting at 4x faster parse performance than the closest
maintained implementation.


Problematic code paths have also been replaced by safer
implementations, solving potential DoS vectors. See
GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2.


Note: the objects returned by the library now have a null
prototype. This is a transparent change for 99.9% of users, and is
one of the most significant contributors to the major performance gains
in this version.


Full Temporal support


Version 1.8.0 brought support for Temporal in stringify;
now the library is also able to emit Temporal objects instead of its own
ad-hoc TomlDate object. It is not enabled by default, but
it will become the default in v2. Enable by setting useLegacyDate:
false in the parser's options.


Better Temporal support in stringify


Temporal support has been improved since it released: Temporal
objects that cannot be represented (such as
Temporal.PlainMonthDay) now throw an error (instead of
silently emitting a bogus object).


A new option has been added to stringify to disallow
Temporal objects that cannot be fully represented in TOML. This includes
ZonedDateTime objects with a IANA timezone attached instead
of a plain offset, and dates with a specific calendar value set. Enable
by setting strictTemporal: true in the options.


Handling of unsafe keys


Since its release the library has been protected against prototype
pollution attacks, setting properties like __proto__ using
safe mechanisms that do not trigger prototype pollution. However, while
the returned objects are safe on their own, they may become problematic
if used carelessly.


Inspired by secure-json-parse, the library now offers a
way to either drop unsafe properties from the returned object, or to
throw an error and reject documents altogether. By default, these
potentially unsafe keys are preserved and returned.


Miscellaneous updates


    

  • Unicode BOM is now gracefully accepted and ignored.
    • 

  • Table array headers are now properly checked again. Reported in #65.
    • 

  • Closed certain gaps where invalid whitespace would be accepted.
Reported in #61.
    • 

  • Bogus local date and local time values with a UTC offset are no
longer accepted.
    • 

  • Certain error messages are more accurate and handle errors at line
boundaries better.
    • 

  • The default export of the lib is now formally deprecated; use a
import * instead. Proposed in #50.
    • 

  • On Node 20+, strings that contain lone surrogates are now normalised
to well-formed strings.
    • 

  • On Node 20+, keys that contain lone surrogates are now
rejected.

feat(stack): run OrioleDB through db.orioledb_version (#6934)

## Summary

**TL;DR:** The experimental local stack can now run OrioleDB through
`db.orioledb_version`, on both the Docker and native runtimes. It uses
the new slim-services OrioleDB release line (`-orioledb`). A
version without a published artifact fails closed, listing the supported
ones.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["db.orioledb_version set"] --> B{"experimental stack?"}
  B -- yes --> C["error: unsupported by the experimental stack"]
  B -- no --> D["Compose: docker.io supabase/postgres:<v>-orioledb"]
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["db.orioledb_version set"] --> B{"OrioleDB pin in catalog?"}
  B -- no --> C["fail closed: lists published versions"]
  B -- yes --> D["stack: slim <v>-orioledb-rN
docker or native"]
  D --> E["db diff / declarative shadow
use the same pin"]
  D --> F["data reuse only within
the OrioleDB line"]
  G["slim-services publishes
<v>-orioledb-r0"] --> H["catalog sync opens
add postgres PR"]
  H --> B
```

### Why

OrioleDB is leaving experimental. The new stack rejected
`db.orioledb_version` with `db.orioledb_version is unsupported by the
experimental stack`. supabase/slim-services#315 now builds and publishes
OrioleDB as its own Postgres release line, next to stock 15 and 17, so
the stack can pin it like any other artifact.

### What changed

- **Catalog sync.** `-orioledb` releases form their own catalog line
(`17-orioledb`).
  - The first publish opens an `add` PR.
  - Later releases upgrade or hotfix that line on their own.
  - An OrioleDB release never touches the stock 17 pin, and the reverse.
  - Legacy tags without `-rN` are ignored.
- **One version resolver.** `db.orioledb_version` (and
`SUPABASE_DB_ORIOLEDB_VERSION`) resolves to `-orioledb` through one
shared resolver. `stack start`, the `db diff` shadow and its cache key,
and the versions output all use it.
  - The setting requires `db.major_version = 17`.
  - An unpinned version fails with the list of published versions.
  - `postgresVersion("17")` still resolves to stock.
- **Data safety.** The ready-marker, `PG_VERSION` and snapshot checks
compare the engine line, not only the major. Stock and OrioleDB data,
snapshots and shadow caches never mix.
- Unmarked data, including data left behind by an interrupted first
start, is refused for an OrioleDB request.
  - The error suggests `supabase stack destroy`.
- Switching `orioledb_version` on a saved stack requires `stack
destroy`, because the stack keeps its database version.
- **`test db`.** Maps OrioleDB to its major for pg_prove.
- **Declarative shadow.** No CLI-side handling: pg-delta's Supabase
profile treats `orioledb` as a platform extension
([supabase/pg-toolbelt#513](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/pull/513)),
so declarative export never emits it and the diff never creates or drops
it. Shipped in pg-delta `1.0.0-alpha.58`, which this PR pins.
- **Compose.** With `SUPABASE_USE_SLIM_IMAGES`, Compose maps
`supabase/postgres:-orioledb` to the pinned slim OrioleDB image.
Unpinned versions stay on docker.io.
- **Docs.** `stack-commands.md`, `SIDE_EFFECTS.md`,
`packages/stack/ARCHITECTURE.md` and ADR 0026.

It also pins the first published OrioleDB release,
`17.11.0.002-orioledb-r0`, added with the catalog sync's `--release`
mode. Later OrioleDB releases arrive through the existing
`slim-release-published` sync.

chore(deps): upgrade effect to 4.0.2 (#6999)

Bumps `effect`, `@effect/platform-bun`, `@effect/platform-node`,
`@effect/platform-node-shared`, `@effect/sql-pg`, and `@effect/vitest`
from `4.0.0-rc.112` to the stable `4.0.2` release. `@effect/tsgo` is
unchanged.

The goal is zero change to CLI behaviour. Every edit is either required
by a removed or renamed API, or restores a behaviour whose upstream
default moved.

## Commit layout

The first three commits are the bump plus two scripted rewrites and can
be skipped by reviewers:

- `effect/unstable/*` import paths moved to `effect/*` (removed upstream
in rc.118,
[effect#8354](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8354)).
- CLI and Config constructors renamed to PascalCase
([effect#7453](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/7453),
[effect#8121](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8121)).

The remaining commits are hand migrations, one topic each.

## Hand migrations

- **node-postgres pool bridge** — `@effect/sql-pg` 4.0 is a native
client and dropped `PgClient.fromPool`
([effect#7426](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/7426)). The
remote database session keeps its own node-postgres pool for the zero
idle timeout, the per-connection role step-down hook, and raw `COPY`
connections, so `db-connection.pool-client.ts` is a small
`SqlClient.make` adapter over that pool with the same statement
execution, cancellation, and error classification the old bridge had.
- **Stack RPC strictness** — parse-option annotations no longer affect
decoding ([effect#8131](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8131))
and the RPC transport passes no parse options, so the initialization
command and `runCommand` payload schemas now reject unknown keys through
a `Record` filter ahead of the struct decode, with the same "Expected no
excess property" wording. Encoding drops `undefined` entries first, so
optional fields passed as explicit `undefined` (for example
`pgProve.workingDir`) still cross the RPC JSON codec as they did with
the plain struct.
- **One statement per query** — the native `@effect/sql-pg` client sends
everything through the extended protocol, which rejects multi-command
strings. The realtime schema bootstrap runs as two statements, and the
generated `ALTER ROLE` / `ALTER DATABASE` batches come back from
Postgres as an array and run one at a time inside the same transaction.
- **Socket addresses, file sizes, encoding, sockets** — server addresses
are `NetAddress.SocketAddress` values, `File.seek` and `File.Info.size`
use `bigint` and `ByteSize`, `Encoding` moved to
`effect/encoding/Base64Url`, and the whole-stack WebSocket test helper
uses the reader and writer pair.
- **`Effect.partition`** returns `[passes, fails]`; the `stack destroy`
handler destructures in that order.
- **Management API contracts** — `packages/api` contracts are
regenerated; the 4.0.2 schema codegen emits code-point length checks and
Unicode-flagged patterns.
- **Config package** — `SchemaAST.Union.mode` moved under `options`,
`ToJsonSchemaOptions.additionalProperties` became `onExcessProperty`,
and regex patterns need the Unicode flag to be exported into JSON Schema
([effect#8482](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8482)). Peer
dependency ranges are untouched and already satisfy 4.0.2.

## Preserved defaults

- The stack's `PgClient.layer` calls pin `idleTimeout: "10 seconds"`;
the default since 4.0.1 is 60 seconds
([effect#8679](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8679)).
- The published JSON Schema files (`@supabase/config` `schema.json` and
`project-schema.json`, mirrored at `apps/docs/public/cli/*.schema.json`)
are byte-identical to the develop build. `toCliConfigJsonSchema` passes
`onExcessProperty: "error"` so structs keep `additionalProperties:
false` ([effect#8147](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8147));
the shared document assembler leaves pattern-keyed records open, as the
generator has no per-schema setting for that; and bucket tables are
modelled so they render as the published object-or-array union.

## Behaviour changes reviewed and accepted

These upstream changes have no configuration knob. Each was checked
against the repo's call sites and judged not user-visible:

- Child-process `kill` and scoped release now wait for the process
group, bounded to one second without `forceKillAfter`
([effect#8018](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8018)). The
stack host, bundled Postgres clients, and containers already set
`forceKillAfter`; other spawn sites can only see up to one extra second
of teardown when a descendant lingers.
- `Effect.cached` treats interruption as abandonment
([effect#8719](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8719)). Every
cached effect in the repo is awaited by a single fiber or forked into an
owning scope, so the shared-interruption semantics do not apply.
- Empty bucket tables under `storage.analytics.buckets` and
`storage.vector.buckets` are modelled as an object-or-array union
instead of `Schema.Struct({})`. Runtime decoding now rejects a primitive
bucket value (`foo = "x"`), which the old schema accepted and ignored;
objects and arrays decode as before.
- HTTP client spans are named after the bare method (`GET` instead of
`http.client GET`), following the OpenTelemetry convention. Nothing in
the repo keys on the old name.
- Generated Management API string length checks count code points
instead of UTF-16 code units, which only differs for characters outside
the Basic Multilingual Plane.

## Patches

- Rebased: the `@effect/platform-node-shared` stdin EPIPE listener, now
against 4.0.2. 4.0.2 still removes the stdin sink's error listener
before the final `end()` flush, so a child that exits before reading its
input raises an uncaught EPIPE on Linux;
[effect#7712](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/7712) and
[effect#7714](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/7714) do not
cover that path.
- Rewritten: the `@effect/vitest` `runTest` patch. Upstream's finalizer
ordering fix
([effect#8154](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/8154)) covers
the abort hook, so the patch now only layers the two behaviours the
stack's `effect-timeout` tests assert on top of it: rejecting with the
pretty errors and reporting a finalizer failure after a timeout.

## Test-only changes

- Stack integration and CLI `db reset` e2e fixtures that seeded data
through `PgClient.layer` with semicolon-joined statements now issue one
statement per call; fixtures that go through `psql` are unchanged.
- The `db reset` e2e fixture reads `count(*)::int`, since the native
client decodes `int8` as `bigint`.

## Follow-ups

- Migrate the remote database session to the native `@effect/sql-pg`
client and delete the pool adapter. That changes result decoding (int8,
timestamps, bytea) across the SQL consumers and needs its own review.

## TL;DR

stops a database helper from being left behind as a `Created` container
when readiness times out mid create

## whats introduced?

the helper is now created by name with `docker create --rm -i` and 
then attached with `docker start --attach --interactive`, so the name
exists before any readiness timeout and `rm -f` always finds it. `create
--rm -i` keeps the `AutoRemove` and `StdinOnce` of `run`, so a dead
owner still ends the helper...

errors. a create the daemon finishes after that timeout is removed again
by name on owner shutdown, and an owner killed between `create` and
`start` leaves a helper the stack sweep on stop and destroy removes.

fix(cli): classify new local stack failures in telemetry (#7044)

## Summary

**TL;DR** Failures from the new local stack (`supabase stack *`, and
stack-backed `db reset`, `db dump`, `db diff`, `test db` and `functions
serve`) now reach telemetry with a cause. Before, most of them were
reported as one fingerprint per error tag with category `unknown`, so
start and destroy failures couldn't be told apart. A port conflict now
counts as user-actionable only when the user pinned the port.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["typed failure
port, pull, timeout"] --> B["StackError
message only"]
  B --> C["…StartError
reason unknown"]
  C --> D["tag:ExperimentalStackStartError
category unknown"]
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["typed failure
port, pull, timeout"] -->|failureKind| B["StackError
kind + reason"]
  B --> C["…StartError
reason stack"]
  C -->|StackError adapter| D["tag:ExperimentalStackStartError:port_conflict
invalid_config"]
```

### Why

Every `@supabase/stack` failure crossed the owner RPC boundary as
message text. The CLI wrapped each one as `reason: "unknown"`, and none
of the `ExperimentalStack*Error` reasons set a fingerprint suffix. As a
result:

- the top new-stack start and destroy errors showed as `unknown`;
- `stack status` "no stack" and real flag errors shared one fingerprint;
- a raw `StackError` that escaped a command was reported as
`tag:unknown`, losing even its tag.

### What changed

- **`@supabase/stack` carries a failure kind.** `failureKind()` derives
a closed `StackFailureKind` from the typed cause chain. It is carried on
`StackError`, each failed composition outcome, the `POST /shutdown`
failure body and the owner readiness line.
- Failure sites that know the cause set the kind explicitly: port
claims, engine command failures, health and startup timeouts, process
exit and stop, artifact preparation, state, owner startup, connection
and exit, and lease conflicts.
- Docker stderr is classified only where the container error is built,
as with the existing retry classifiers.
- **The wire field is an open string.** An older client that decodes a
newer owner's error ignores kinds it doesn't know instead of rejecting
the response.
- **Port provenance.** `port-conflict` (user-actionable) is reserved for
a port requested by number, i.e. set in `config.toml` or a
`SUPABASE_*_PORT` override. The stack's own allocation reports
`port-allocation` (internal bug):
- auto-assigned ports, including a saved auto assignment that is now
taken;
  - native backend port collisions;
  - Docker publish refusals, since Docker chooses the host port.
- **A typed `StackError` adapter in the CLI.** It lives in
`error-actionability.ts` and checks, in order:
  1. the client `reason`;
  2. the `kind`;
  3. the first failed outcome's kind;
  4. otherwise `:unclassified`.
- **Per-reason fingerprints.** Every new-stack command error reason,
plus `FunctionsServeStackError`, has its own fingerprint suffix (for
example `:not_found`, `:flags`, `:confirmation`). A `stack` reason
classifies through its wrapped cause, so wrapped CLI errors such as
`DbSetupError` keep their own classification.
- **Stack-backed db and functions wrappers** keep the stack cause, so
the real failure shows through: `LocalDbRunningError`, `db reset`, `db
dump`, `db diff`, declarative sync, `test db` and `functions serve`.
- **Engine command failures** are classified as `runtime_crash` /
`engine_command` rather than `invalid_config`.
- **Unused internal CLI reasons are removed:** `registry`, `port`,
`artifact` and `impossible-state`.

### Reviewer notes

- **Dashboards:** fingerprint values change for these errors. A query
matching `tag:ExperimentalStackStartError` exactly needs a prefix match
now.
- **`functions serve` edge case:** on a stack with no API service it
still binds the CLI's default API port, so a conflict there reports as
user-actionable. That number also forms the served `SUPABASE_URL` before
the instance exists, so it is left as is.
- **Not covered here** (both pre-existing, for every command): parse
errors (an unknown flag or unexpected argument) and Ctrl+C send no
`cli_command_executed` event.

ci(release): gate hotfix pull requests into main (#7050)

Linear: [CLI-2442](https://linear.app/supabase/issue/CLI-2442)

Hotfix PR gating, the first of three PRs that complete the hotfix flow
on top of the branch and release work from #7038. A hotfix is a
`hotfix/*` PR into `main` with a `fix`, `perf`, or `revert` title;
squash-merging publishes the next stable patch and the existing sync
carries it back to `develop`.

- **Check Deploy** always runs and reports. On the scheduled `develop`
promotion it succeeds. On `hotfix/*` heads it requires the title to
start with `fix`, `perf`, or `revert`, with an optional scope and no
`!`, and the failure message says what to change. Any other head fails,
and so does a fork head on either path: hotfixes come from this
repository. The job is named so it can become a required status check on
`main` later; because `main` has no App bypass, the promotion's head SHA
must carry a real success for the deploy fast-forward push to pass.
- **Release Smoke Test** triggers on hotfix PRs into `main` and runs the
shared release pipeline with `dry_run: true`, restoring the
build-and-smoke rehearsal that beta normally provides. Dispatch inputs
keep their defaults. Runs are per-PR concurrent with cancel-in-progress,
and fork pull requests are skipped since their token cannot hold the
permissions the shared workflow declares.
- **Release dispatch guard**: a non-dry-run stable release can only be
dispatched from `main`. The `hotfix/*` exemption existed for the manual
rehearsal, which this PR makes automatic. @Coly010, was a real stable
publish from an unmerged hotfix branch intended? If so, say so and I
will restore it.

Verified on a scratch repository: with a ruleset requiring only this
check on `main`, a direct push of a deploy PR head and of a hotfix PR
head both passed once the job had reported on the head SHA, and a push
with no check run was rejected (rule suites 4418391424 and 4418634505).

separate PR.

description:
Release v1.20.0

Notable Changes

  • Remove the Terraform deployment engine. bundle.engine: terraform and DATABRICKS_BUNDLE_ENGINE=terraform now error, and a failed migration of existing Terraform state is reported as an error instead of falling back to Terraform. To keep deploying with Terraform, use Databricks CLI v1.19.x. (#6888, #6889)

CLI

  • databricks aitools install now supports Kiro, installing Databricks agent skills into its skills directory. (#6908)
  • Fixed databricks api corrupting integers larger than 2^53 (such as job and pipeline ids) — request bodies and responses now preserve them exactly. (#6884)
  • Added --auth-mode and --set ..authMode=obo|sp|both to databricks apps init so AppKit resources can be accessed on behalf of the user, by the service principal, or both. The default stays service principal. (#6886)
  • databricks apps init now requires a value for every field a service principal resource binding references, prompting for missing values in an interactive terminal and otherwise failing with the --set key to use, instead of creating a project with unset variables. (#6903)
  • Add databricks apps init --package-manager to select the package manager for Node.js templates. Infer the default quietly from template lockfiles and AppKit version, check prerequisites before creating files, and preserve template formatting and pnpm version pins. (#6902)
  • Select npm or pnpm from packageManager declarations and lockfiles for apps validate and project validation during apps deploy. (#6892)
  • Fix auth docker host reporting the credential helper as configured when its executable is missing from PATH. (#6880)
  • Warn when the CLI binary was built more than 6 months ago and recommend updating. (#6898)

AI Runtime

  • Add an experimental rank-partitioned container images to AI Runtime jobs. (#6841)
  • Support snapshot fields directly under code_source without requiring type or a nested snapshot block. (#6927)
  • Map AIR priority and Unity Catalog image fields when converting run configurations to bundles. (#6905)
  • Add workspace backend validation to air run --dry-run. (#6934)

Bundles

  • Warn that bundle.terraform is deprecated and has no effect since the Terraform deployment engine was removed. (#6940)
  • Direct engine now detects and applies an explicitly configured zero-value boolean or float (e.g. gcp_attributes.use_preemptible_executors: false, azure_attributes.spot_bid_max_price: 0) added to a resource first deployed without the field, matching the existing handling of an explicit integer zero. (#6882)
  • Fix bundle deployment migrate failing with "no such file or directory" when the Terraform state has no resources or the configuration no longer declares any of them. (#6958)
  • bundle run and pipelines run now send the per-update development parameter for pipelines in development mode targets. Setting development on a pipeline is deprecated and now emits a warning; use mode: development instead. (#6863)
  • Remove the hidden bundle debug terraform command. (#6933)
  • Add support for run_as.group_name at the bundle and target levels for jobs and pipelines. (#6676)
  • Fix recreating a secret scope that was deleted outside of the bundle with the direct deployment engine. (#6970)
  • Accept title-case booleans (True/False, as rendered by Azure Pipelines) for boolean variables, and accept the same boolean strings (yes/no, on/off, ...) in Python bundles as in YAML. (#6942)

Dependency Updates

  • Bump github.com/databricks/databricks-sdk-go from v0.182.0 to v0.185.0. (#6928)

air: bound submission config validation timeout and retry (#6994)

## What did you change, and why?

- Bound preflight validation for normal `databricks air run` submissions
to one request with a five-second deadline after SDK credential setup.
On `main`, this path uses the SDK's retry policy and can wait for the
configured retry window, which defaults to five minutes, on retryable
failures.
- Warn and continue when validation is unavailable because the endpoint
is disabled or missing, the service returns HTTP 408, 429, or 5xx, the
request or token refresh reaches its deadline, transport fails, or the
response cannot be read or decoded. Submission still receives
authoritative downstream validation, so temporary preflight
unavailability should not block it.
- Continue blocking field-validation errors, HTTP 400/401/403 and other
caller errors, definitive authentication failures, request setup
failures, and user cancellation. These failures are actionable or
explicitly initiated and should not be treated as service
unavailability.
- Preserve the validation request's SDK authentication, routing,
user-agent, and trace headers, and add a release note for the bounded
behavior.

## How do you know it works?

- Added focused coverage for the single-attempt limit, timeout, warning
and error classification, OAuth refresh and rejection, response-body
failures, malformed responses, and cancellation.
- Passed `go test ./cmd/air`, focused race tests, `go vet ./cmd/air`,
and GolangCI lint with Staticcheck disabled.
- Verified authenticated workspace dry runs and a real A10G workload
through successful completion and log streaming.

Translate paths in job environment_variables files (#6985)

The v0.185.0 SDK bump (#6928) added `environment_variables` to jobs.
Each entry's `spec.files` lists `.env` files that tasks load at runtime,
which the backend reads only from `/Workspace/...` or `/Volumes/...`
paths. Relative paths in that list were passed through untranslated, so
a path relative to the bundle would not resolve.

This adds a job-level path rewrite pattern for
`resources.jobs.*.environment_variables[*].spec.files[*]`, translating
relative paths to their deployed workspace locations like other job file
paths. Absolute `/Volumes` and `/Workspace` paths pass through
unchanged, and jobs using `git_source` continue to skip path translation

description:
ssh: don't report a failed handover when the session ends mid-handover (#6976)

## Why

`TestQuickHandover` failed in the merge queue:
https://github.com/databricks/cli/actions/runs/37613006327/job/112764757499

The cause is a race at session end. A handover can wait for the old
websocket to close when the session ends. Teardown then closes that
websocket itself. The receiving loop sent the read error (`use of closed
network connection`) to `initiateHandover`. The client handover
goroutine then returned `ErrHandoverFailed`.

This also affects real sessions, not only the test:

- A clean `ssh` exit during a handover reported `ErrHandoverFailed`,
because no other error existed.
- When the session ended with a real error, the handover error could
reach the errgroup first. `normalizeProxyError` then changed it to
`nil`, so the real error was lost.
- Resumable sessions logged a false "recovering through session
reattachment" line. A ready tick could then start a new handover for a
session that was ending.

## Changes

- `proxy.go`: During a handover, the receiving loop now decides in this
order:
1. A normal close completes the swap, as before. This is also true when
the session is ending, so teardown closes the replacement websocket
gracefully and a resumable peer does not wait for a reattach.
2. If the read fails after the proxy context is cancelled, teardown
broke the read. The loop sends `ctx.Err()` to the handover initiator.
Before, it sent the read error.
  3. Any other read error is a dropped websocket, as before.
- `client.go`: If `initiateHandover` returns `context.Canceled`, the
handover goroutine returns `nil`. The result of `proxy.start` then
decides how the session ended. The check comes after the dial-failed
branch, because a failed dial never changes the live connection. It
comes before the resumable branch, so both modes stop the same way.
- A real handover failure, for example a handover timeout
(`DeadlineExceeded`) or a dropped websocket, still returns
`ErrHandoverFailed`.

## Tests

- `TestSessionEndDuringHandover`: the handover dial goes to a server
that never answers, so the handover stays in progress. Then the session
ends. The test has 4 cases: a clean exit and a source error, in
non-resumable and resumable mode. Each case checks the session result.
It also checks that no new handover starts after the session ends.
- Without the `proxy.go` change, all 4 cases failed in most of 10 runs.
- Without the `client.go` change, the source-error and resumable cases
failed in most of 10 runs.
- `TestServerEOFDuringHandoverIsACleanExit`: sshd's stdout ends while
the server reads the client's close acknowledgment for a handover. The
client must exit cleanly.
- `TestClientEOFDuringHandoverReleasesServer`: the client's input ends
while the client holds the server's handover close. The server must end
the session at once, and not wait for a reattach.
- Both EOF tests failed in 20 of 20 runs on earlier versions of this PR,
and passed with the base code. They run on all platforms.
- `TestHandoverDialCanceledKeepsHandingOver`: a dial that fails with
`context.Canceled` does not stop later handovers.
- The new tests, `TestQuickHandover`, and
`TestHandoverDialFailureKeepsSessionAlive` passed in 30 of 30 runs with
`-race`. The `experimental/ssh/internal/proxy`, `internal/client`, and
`internal/server` packages pass with `-race`.

The test client now uses a `Done` channel. With it, a test can wait for
`RunClientProxy` to return before `Cleanup` closes the input pipe.

## Known limits

These edge cases exist on `main` too, and this PR does not change them.
Each needs a teardown during the short window of a handover, which runs
once every 30 minutes:

- If teardown breaks the read before the peer's handover close arrives,
the initiator closes the replacement websocket without a close frame. A
resumable peer then waits for a reattach.
- During a handover, the receiving loop treats any normal close as the
handover close, including the peer's `"finished"` close.

release-prs: sync winget-pkgs fork before publishing to winget (#6979)

## Changes

The `publish-to-winget-pkgs` job failed for v1.20.0 with:

```
eng-dev-ecosystem-bot does not have the correct permissions to execute `CreateRef`
```

This error is misleading — it is **not** a token/permissions problem.
komac's `update --submit` creates the PR branch *in the
eng-dev-ecosystem-bot fork* pointing at **upstream's HEAD commit**.
GitHub's `createRef` requires that commit object to be accessible in the
fork; when the fork's default branch has drifted far behind upstream,
GitHub refuses and surfaces the misleading permissions error (see
[komac#1142](https://github.com/russellbanks/Komac/issues/1142)).

The fork was kept in sync by [pull[bot]](https://github.com/apps/pull),
which GitHub [suspended globally on
2026-09-30](https://github.com/wei/pull/issues/674). With no syncing,
the fork drifted thousands of commits behind over the following week and
the publish failed. Manually syncing the fork and re-running fixed it.

This adds a `komac sync-fork` step before the publish step so the fork's
default branch is fast-forwarded to upstream on every release, removing
the dependency on pull[bot]. `komac sync-fork` reuses the same
`KOMAC_FORK_OWNER` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` env as the publish step and no-ops
when the fork is already current.

## Tests

~N/A — release workflow change, gated on `!inputs.dry_run` like the
other komac steps.~

Triggered the workflow off the PR branch
https://github.com/databricks/cli/actions/runs/37635730741/job/112841336462
when https://github.com/eng-dev-ecosystem-bot/winget-pkgs was 4 commits
behind -> succeeded and synced the master branch. (publish step is
no-op/idempotent)

description:
Fix generate-clijson for a blobless Universe checkout (#6929)

**Human TL;DR:** Fix generate-clijson task after I ran into issues
during the latest SDK bump

---

## Changes

Fix two pre-existing bugs in the `generate-clijson` task recipe that
only surface when the task is actually run (it is excluded from CI's
reproducible-generation check, so neither has been caught):

- The pinned `go-task` embedded shell (`mvdan.cc/sh` v3.13.1) only
accepts `EXIT`/`ERR` in `trap`, so `trap '...' EXIT HUP INT TERM` aborts
the recipe with `trap: HUP: invalid signal specification` (exit 2). Use
`EXIT` only.
- `git clone --shared` does not carry over partial-clone/promisor
config, so when `UNIVERSE_DIR` is a blobless (`filter=blob:none`) clone
the temp checkout fails with `cannot read object` for every file blob
not already in the shared object store. Mirror the source's promisor
config onto the temp clone's `origin` (pointed at the upstream remote)
so missing blobs are lazily fetched during checkout. No-op for a full
clone.

## Why

Both were hit while running an SDK bump against a blobless `~/universe`
partial clone. Keeping `generate-clijson` runnable in that setup avoids
a manual blob backfill before every bump.

## Tests

The `trap EXIT` change was exercised end-to-end: with it applied,
`./task generate-clijson` runs through the genkit Bazel build and
regenerates `.codegen/cli.json` on this setup, whereas the unpatched
recipe aborts immediately with `invalid signal specification`.

The promisor-config change is not covered by an automated test. It
mirrors the exact partial-clone config the Universe checkout itself uses
(`remote.origin.promisor=true` plus `partialclonefilter`), so missing
blobs resolve through the same lazy-fetch path; a full (non-partial)
`UNIVERSE_DIR` is unaffected because the block only runs when the source
has a `partialclonefilter`.

fix(quota): include UTC offset in refresh timestamps (#1211)

## Summary

Fixes #1209.

`kaggle quota` can display `refreshAt` without a timezone marker:

```text
2026-10-03T00:00:00
```

The timestamp represents UTC, but users could interpret it as local
time. The SDK returns this timestamp as a datetime without timezone
information, so calling `.isoformat()` omits the UTC offset.

## Fix

Attach UTC to quota refresh timestamps that have no timezone information
before formatting them. The output now includes an explicit offset:

```text
2026-10-03T00:00:00+00:00
```

Existing timezone offsets are preserved, and missing refresh times
remain blank.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for table output, both CSV options, and JSON
output using:

- Timestamps without timezone information.
- UTC timestamps.
- Timestamps with a non-UTC offset.
- Missing timestamps.

The four subcases for timestamps without timezone information failed
before the fix and pass afterward.

Ran:

```text
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_quota.py -v
```

All quota tests pass.

I saw that the underlying issue has also been filed in the SDK repo.
This PR addresses the CLI output while preserving existing timezone
information. Happy to defer to an SDK fix if that’s the preferred
approach.

Logseq 2.0.2 Beta brings smoother editing, faster startup, and more reliable everyday workflows to the DB version.

Join the iOS TestFlight beta, 2.0.2 is currently under App Store review.

Web app: https://app.logseq.com/

Features

  • Gallery cards can now use URL properties as covers.
  • Added a "Clear heading" slash command.
  • Improved video embeds, with resizable desktop players and clickable YouTube timestamps.

Thanks

  • Special thanks to our community PR contributors! Your fixes, performance improvements, translations, and careful reviews helped make this beta better. Contributors include @yuxi-liu-wired, @ChipNowacek, @Mancn-Xu, @hahaArthur17, @maksym-dilanian, @qwist1233-cpu, and many others.
  • A heartfelt thank-you to everyone testing the DB beta. Your bug reports, reproduction steps, feedback, and retesting of fixes have been invaluable. Thank you for helping us improve Logseq with your real-world graphs and workflows!

Fixed issues

Ordered by impact on data integrity, reliability, and everyday workflows.

  1. Preserve unsaved edits: Save pending text before following page or block references, switching blocks, or setting Deadline/Scheduled. Pasting multiple blocks no longer lets a stale editor buffer erase the first pasted title.
  2. Restore deleted content with undo/redo: Restore deleted blocks and pages that reference each other, along with property schemas and values. Undoing block moves now preserves their original order and nested structure.
  3. Keep block trees intact when copying or moving: Selecting an ancestor together with its descendants no longer pulls grandchildren out of their subtree. Copy/paste preserves the original child blocks, and embed actions operate on the embed rather than its source.
  4. Keep graph and asset downloads running: One failed asset download no longer stops the remaining asset queue or fails the graph download. Sync also keeps property-value replacements together instead of splitting them across requests.
  5. Fix Windows installation: Fix the NSIS installer crash affecting Windows 11 24H2 and newer, so the desktop app can be installed normally.
  6. Improve file-to-DB import fidelity: Preserve headings, icons, journal timestamps, and PDF annotation identities/order. Asset links in property values are converted into asset references, and same-title classes and properties remain distinct.
  7. Correct scheduled dates and repeating tasks: Deadline/Scheduled repeats now advance in the local calendar. Monthly repeats no longer drift permanently after a shorter month; date filters use local days, and clearing dates removes stale journal references.
  8. Prevent query errors from crashing the graph: Incomplete query syntax, invalid regular expressions, and query-function rendering errors are isolated. Query-builder filters again show property/tag names and include custom Status and Priority choices.
  9. Fix property editing and choice selection: Selected node values remain visible in property pickers, choice identities resolve consistently, and configuration toggles save the newly selected value. Empty multi-value slots and date values can be cleared without errors.
  10. Restore readable search results and references: Resolve UUID references in search titles, breadcrumbs, and nested page references. References to deleted nodes remain visible as broken links, and opening search no longer clears its results.
  11. Restore settings and HTML publishing: Settings can be saved when config.edn is missing or invalid, and the first export.css edit creates the file correctly. HTML exports no longer open as a blank page and honor the configured home page.
  12. Make desktop editing and keyboard input reliable: Clicks during scrolling now open the editor. A click after Escape or Shift+Up/Down keeps the newly opened editor, and fixes cover international dead-key input and IME confirmation in search.
  13. Fix Android popup and layout issues: Nested popups reuse the presented native sheet, sheet dismissal avoids re-entry, and the layout respects the status-bar safe area. Mobile cloud-graph download and sync triggers work again.

Enhancements

  • Faster startup and smoother editing: Improved desktop startup, journal loading, large-page rendering, table scrolling, and search, with fewer unnecessary updates while typing.
  • Better everyday workflows: Improved flashcard practice, date and repeating-task handling, international keyboard input, plugin APIs, CLI behavior, and translations.

enhance(rtc): support E2EE graphs in semantic API and PATs (#13671)

* enhance(rtc): support E2EE graphs in semantic API and PATs

PATs can now be created for E2EE-encrypted graphs and the semantic API
serves them end to end:

- Edge helpers: GET /e2ee/public-keys, POST /e2ee/encrypt and
  POST /e2ee/decrypt so agents don't reimplement transit+AES-GCM.
- Encrypt accepts either a caller-supplied AES key (canonical
  [iv ciphertext] package) or no key, producing an RSA-envelope
  package with an ephemeral AES key wrapped to every member's RSA
  public key — agents need no secrets to write.
- A graph-scoped PAT may GET /e2ee/graphs/:id/aes-key for its own
  graph to bootstrap decryption (also exposes a base64 form of the
  wrapped key); all other /e2ee index routes stay 403 for PATs.
- Writes to E2EE graphs must submit encrypted packages: title/body
  fields that are not valid ciphertext return 400. Reads return
  ciphertext unchanged.
- Page create skips title validation and namespace splitting for
  encrypted titles, and [[ref]] extraction is skipped on E2EE
  graphs since titles are opaque.
- listGraphs/graphGet expose graph-e2ee? instead of filtering
  E2EE graphs out.
- Client-side decrypt understands RSA-envelope packages by
  unwrapping with the user's RSA private key.
- Settings > Encryption shows the public key and reveals the
  private key only after password verification; the PAT graph
  picker lists E2EE graphs with an (E2EE) label.

* fix(rtc): pass index e2ee flag to DO and harden semantic input validation

The DO-side e2ee write gate relied solely on the graph DB's
:logseq.kv/graph-rtc-e2ee? kv, which is only populated at RTC upload.
Freshly created encrypted graphs (index flag already set) therefore
accepted plaintext writes and ciphertext titles hit page-name
validation. The edge now forwards the authoritative index flag as a
graph-e2ee search param and the DO gates on kv-or-param.

Also fixes malformed inputs returning 500 instead of 400:
malformed JSON bodies (body-clj swallows parse errors so existing
missing-field checks fire), non-string titles (seq throws on numbers),
and non-sequential blocks/entries collections. Blocks title collection
no longer misuses concat as a transducer.

* enhance(rtc): serve semantic api on local node adapter

Routes /openapi.json and /api/* through the same worker dispatch in
the local node adapter, with a LOGSEQ_SYNC_DO stand-in that forwards
to the local graph context and unlimited rate limiters, so the
semantic REST API can be exercised end-to-end against a local server.

* fix(rtc): clean up lint warnings in e2ee helpers

* fix(rtc): decode transit private key before password reveal

the raw message, the same on every backend, instead of mail-parser's
own model: address lists as `{name, email}`, decoded subject, RFC 3339
date, ids without angle brackets, list headers, bodies decoded to UTF-8,

An agent handed a creative-mode share link (/page/) and asked to read or
summarize it never reached +export: the lark-apps description did not mention

Re-type that envelope as the same permission_denied error the 403 branch

description:
Don't stall the Find Full Text queue on a failing download

A file URL returning a server error was retried for up to an hour inside
the download, and a 429 or Retry-After was waited out there too. Since
the queue processes one item at a time, that blocked every other
selected item. Throttling now goes to Find Full Text's own per-domain
handling, as it did before 10.0, which also needed to read Retry-After
from a fetch Response and parse HTTP-date values.

https://forums.zotero.org/discussion/133703/
product_or_resource: Don't stall the Find Full Text queue on a failing download

description:
Added

  • Formatting in direct messages: send_message takes formatting: true (CLI: send --format), same markers and same off-by-default rule as for groups and notes.
  • MCP tool annotations on all 81 tools (read-only / destructive / idempotent / open-world hints and a title), kept in one table (tool_annotations.py) and guarded by a test so a new tool can't ship unclassified.

Changed

  • Tool descriptions rewritten for every tool: each parameter is now explained in the description text (before, 106 of 257 were only in the JSON schema), with when-to-use-instead guidance for sibling tools, side effects and reversibility, and the exact result shape. Guarded by tests. Several old descriptions made claims the code does not back up (search "ranked by relevance", attachments "returned as base64", "no admin list" etc.); those are corrected.

Fixed

  • get_avatar never worked for phone numbers. signal-cli's getAvatar takes profile, contact or groupId; we sent recipient, which ends in a NullPointerException. It now asks for the contact's profile photo first and falls back to the locally set contact avatar.
  • get_avatar and get_sticker always returned an empty image. signal-cli returns the image in a field called data; the code read one called base64, which does not exist. Tests had mocked the wrong shape, so they passed.
  • get_profile returned only a number and UUID. It used getUserStatus (registration state). It now reads the profile (names, about) from the contact list, including non-contacts.
  • README and schedule-send help said the background service sends scheduled messages. It does not. Only run_scheduled_messages / signal-mcp run-scheduled send them; both texts now say so.

Added

  • Formatting in group messages: send_group_message takes formatting: true (CLI: send-group --format) and turns **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `mono` and ||spoiler|| into real Signal formatting, same as notes. Off by default so text with literal asterisks or backticks is never changed behind your back. With it, @mention offsets refer to the text as written (markers included) and are remapped automatically; all style and mention ranges are guaranteed to stay inside the sent text, which Signal Android 8.15+ requires (it silently drops messages with out-of-range styles, signal-cli#2075).

Fixed

  • signal-mcp history and signal-mcp search printed bare phone numbers and truncated group ids even though the README promised names. They now show contact/profile names and group names (as conversations and the MCP tools already did).

Changed

  • PyPI package metadata: a clearer one-line description, keywords, classifiers and project links (homepage, issues, changelog).
  • README rewritten around what you get first: example conversation, real terminal output, quick start, a "what you can ask" table, a privacy section, troubleshooting, and the previously undocumented scheduling/webhook tools and CLI commands.

Closes the gap between signal-cli and the MCP tools: a command-by-command and field-by-field comparison found that signal-mcp discarded most incoming-message data and exposed only part of several commands' options.

Added

  • Incoming messages keep everything signal-cli reports: mentions (plus body_resolved with @name in place of the placeholder; UTF-16 offsets handled), text_styles, link previews, full quote (author, text), voice_note, sticker, payment, shared contacts, polls (poll_create / poll_vote / poll_terminate), pins/unpins, story replies, and event flags. Stored in one new nullable extras JSON column, added by a guarded migration (existing databases keep working).
  • Group member labels: list_groups returns each member's label / label_emoji; update_group sets your own (member_label, member_label_emoji). Also exposed: pending, requesting and banned members, permissions, invite link, termination state, and a group_id filter.
  • update_group: avatar, ban/unban, reset invite link, the three permission settings. create_group takes an avatar.
  • terminate_group (new, irreversible, requires confirm: true) and send_story (new).
  • Contacts and profile: nickname, note, username, archived/hidden/unregistered and more on contacts; update_contact (given/family/nick names, note), update_profile (given/family name, about emoji, MobileCoin address), remove_contact (forget, hide), get_user_status by username, typing indicators in groups. list_contacts / find_contact take all_recipients, and the name cache now uses it, so group members who are not in your address book resolve to their profile names instead of a bare UUID.
  • Sending: link previews, voice-note flag, quoted text/mentions/styles, no_urgent, notify_self, end_session, send by username, story replies; max_messages and ignore_* for receive_*.
  • get_attachment falls back to signal-cli's getAttachment when the file is not in the local folder.

Fixed

  • Received attachments were never copied. signal-cli's filename is the sender's original name, not a path; the file lives in ~/.local/share/signal-cli/attachments/. The store held 0 attachment rows next to 60 files on disk. Now copied by id (path-traversal safe) and the id is kept.
  • Replies sent an empty quote. signal-cli builds the quote text from quoteMessage; replies now look the original up in the local store.
  • leave_group could not work for a sole admin (signal-cli requires naming a successor).
  • update_group(link_mode="reset") sent a value signal-cli rejects; it now sends resetLink.
  • Typing "stop" never stopped typing, list_identities ignored its number filter, and update_profile's name was silently dropped (signal-cli only reads givenName).
  • Incoming remote/admin deletes were stored as empty messages. They now flag the original (remote_deleted, admin_deleted_by) and keep your local copy.

Changed

  • A contact's display name prefers the Signal nickname, then the contact name, then the profile name.

Found by running Clio Coder against a real Zulip organization. A local model repeated successful sends and posted as the user while presenting itself as the bot. Anyone in the organization could also steer a watcher on the owner's machine by mentioning the bot.

uv tool install zulipchat-mcp==0.7.6

Security

  • Owner-only bot inbox. Mention and direct-message polling now returns only senders admitted by --mention-allow / ZULIPCHAT_MENTION_ALLOW.
    • The default admits only the configured owner.
    • A list of emails and numeric user IDs adds senders.
    • everyone restores the old behavior.
    • Other senders appear in ignored_unauthorized with IDs and no content, and the cursor still advances past them.
    • Invalid entries fail startup.
  • The inbox never returns the bot's own messages, so a reply that mentions the bot cannot become new work.

Added

  • poll_agent_events(direct_messages=True) reads direct and group-direct messages to the bot, with the same durable inbox and cursor as channel mentions. Each event includes reply_to.
  • send_message(as_bot=True) sends one message as the bot over stdio.
  • Every tool advertises MCP annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint, title), derived from the read-only profile.

Fixed

  • send_message suppresses an identical repeat of a send that succeeded within the last two minutes and returns the original message_id. Results report sent_as and a UTC timestamp.
  • Link-preview updates no longer delete a stored mention or direct message before the host reads it.
  • The packaged skill teaches sending once, speaking as the bot, and polling once per turn with a cursor.

Verified live

Verified against a real organization with Clio Coder. Owner-only filtering held on real direct messages, a non-owner's question was withheld, and a channel mention got exactly one reply as the bot with an advancing cursor.
